product.name: Fenland Celery
product.detailed_description: Fenland Celery is a unique white winter celery grown exclusively in the rich, dark soils of the Fens. With its distinctively sweet, nutty flavour, it still tastes just as it did when first grown in Victorian times. Perfect in hearty soups and stews, paired with creamy blue cheese, served fresh in seasonal salads, or enjoyed simply with a cheese board and dips, Fenland Celery is loved by chefs and home cooks alike. A true seasonal treat, it’s only available for 8 short weeks each year – so enjoy it while you can! Grown using traditional methods passed down through generations, this seasonal delicacy has a rich heritage and a flavour like no other. Recognised with Protected Geographical Indication (PGI) status, Fenland Celery joins an exclusive group of British foods celebrated for their quality. Its sweet, nutty flavour and crisp texture come from the unique growing method known as earthing up, where the soil is carefully banked around the celery plants to protect them from frost and naturally blanch the stems to their signature pale colour. Discover more about its history, growing methods, and explore a range of delicious recipe ideas at www.fenlandcelery.com.
product.features: Traditional Fenland celery as it used to taste!, Deliciously nutty & mellow!, 100% English grown exclusively in the Fenlands, In season & only available October to December, Grown using only Fenland water
product.further_description: For the traditional way to prepare celery for the cheese board and further recipe ideas please visit: fenlandcelery.com
product.brand_marketing: Fenland celery dates back to the Victorian times when the crop was specially grown in the Fens for sale in the Christmas markets in London. It was extremely popular and became a feature of the Victorian Londoner's Christmas dinner. Cambridgeshire producer G's Fresh revived Fenland celery a decade ago. After bringing the 150 year-old crop home to London's prestigious New Covent Garden Market, Fenland celery quickly attracted a loyal following of chefs and foodies. Now Fenland celery is available nationwide, through good retailers. Today's Fenland celery looks much the same as it did 150 years ago. Look out for its leafy top and pale white stick, cut to a point by hand, as dictated by tradition.

product.recipes: Fenland Celery Braised in White Wine, Cream & Thyme Serve as a side with roast chicken. Serves 4-6 as a side dish Preparation Time: 10mins Cooking Time: 1 hour 30-45 mins What you'll need 1 bunch Fenland celery, separated into stems Small bunch fresh thyme, woody stalks removed 150ml white wine 250ml double cream 1 clove garlic, crushed Salt & freshly ground black pepper 25g butter What to do: 1: Preheat the oven to 180°C. 2: Use a potato peeler to take a thin slice down the outer edge of each Fenland celery stem to remove any tough strings. Cut each stem in half and for the thicker stems, cut in half down the length too. 3: Lay the celery end to end in a rectangular baking dish, tucking in the thyme sprigs. 4: In a jug, stir together the wine, cream and crushed garlic. Season generously with salt and freshly ground black pepper. 5: Pour the wine and cream over the celery and dot the butter over the top. Loosely cover with foil and bake in the over for an hour or so until the celery is just tender when pierced with the point of a knife. 6: Remove the foil and bake for a further 30-45 minutes until the top is golden and bubbling
